Scoop app manifest for tobby. Scoop reads a manifest named after the
app from a bucket repository, so the published copy of this file would
be bucket/tobby.json in a bucket of ours; this repository holds the
template, and the release workflow renders it and attaches it to the
GitHub release. Nothing is pushed to a bucket by that workflow — see
the scoop job in .github/workflows/release.yml for why the last mile is
deliberately a human step.
JSON has no comment syntax; Scoop reserves the '##' property for
exactly this purpose and ignores it when installing, which is why this
header is a string array rather than the comment block every other
packaging file in this repository carries.
Placeholders match the convention of packaging/homebrew/tobby.rb and
the winget manifests: version 0.0.0, and sixty-four zeros for each
hash. Both are rewritten at release time from the SHA256SUMS that run
produced and that the SLSA provenance covers (ADR-0011) — never
recomputed from a re-download, which would only attest to whatever the
network returned.
Windows is a validated target, not an afterthought: NFR-001 requires
the single static binary on Windows for both architectures and NFR-018
puts the whole mirror-mode workflow inside the validated Windows scope.
Scoop is the package manager the operators of those mirror
workstations tend to already have, and it installs per-user with no
administrator rights — which is frequently the only kind of install
available on a managed workstation.
The '#/tobby.exe' URL fragment is Scoop's rename-on-download: the
release asset is architecture-qualified so that six binaries can share
one release page, but the command an operator types is 'tobby', so the
file is stored under that name and 'bin' shims it accordingly.
checkver and autoupdate let a bucket track new releases without a
push from this repository. autoupdate reads the release's own
SHA256SUMS and extracts the digest for the exact asset name, so an
automated bump inherits the same provenance-covered checksums a manual
one would.
description: Secure artifact fetch-and-relocate tool with an embedded OCI registry. Tobby fetches OCI assets — container images, Helm charts, AI models, and files — and carries them across isolated network zones, from connected, through restricted, down to fully air-gapped environments.
